features.name: Louisiana Purchase
features.end_is: last day of the stretch on which the U.S. land is the same

source.dataset: Computed by Parchment (scripts/derive-pieces.mjs) from the Newberry Library's polygons: the land the U.S. polygons gained on the acquisition's day, outside the 1783 domain, credited to its last entry and still U.S. land on the map's date; nothing drawn

acquisition.label: bought
acquisition.name: Louisiana Purchase (1803)
acquisition.source: Statehood Campaigns: Deck Outline (2026-11-18), Taxonomy 1; Office of the Historian, "Louisiana Purchase"
acquisition.note: $15 million. Newberry's la_purchase: "boundaries were not clearly defined but unquestionably included the western half of the Mississippi drainage basin." From the deck outline; not yet reviewed by the owner.

acquisition.label: joined
acquisition.name: Texas (1845)
acquisition.instrument: Joint resolution of 1 March 1845, accepted by the Texas convention 4 July 1845
acquisition.source: Statehood Campaigns: Deck Outline (2026-11-18), Taxonomy 1; Texas State Library
acquisition.note: With the claims Texas sold in 1850 (9 Stat. 446): in New Mexico, Colorado, Kansas, Oklahoma and Wyoming that land is the Texas piece. From the deck outline; not yet reviewed by the owner.

acquisition.label: won
acquisition.name: Mexican Cession (1848)
acquisition.note: The treaty ended a war (the $15 million paid does not make it a purchase under the taxonomy's rule). From the deck outline; not yet reviewed by the owner.
